verdict.rationale: Fivetran's own Connector SDK lets data engineers develop custom Python connectors. Its AI coding-agent plugins, which run in local CLIs such as Claude Code, Codex CLI and Gemini CLI, explicitly let users 'build, test, and deploy connectors', which implies a pre-deployment test loop. Nothing in the evidence documents running a pipeline locally or writing to a lightweight local destination, and the core managed connectors have no local mode at all. missing for 10: documented local run/debug command, a lightweight local destination (e.g., file or embedded DB) for testing, any isolation from production destinations, hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I run and test a pipeline locally against a lightweight destination before it touches production

citations.quote: These skills let you build, test, and deploy connectors using natural language prompts.
Fivetran’s Connector SDK allows you to develop a custom data connector using Python and deploy it as an extension of Fivetran.
